items.title: Philanthropic giving summary for a founder with a private foundation
items.summary: Summary of $412,000 of family philanthropy: $250,000 of foundation grants, $110,000 of donor-advised fund grants funded with appreciated company stock, and $52,000 of direct gifts. Giving in shares avoided about $96,000 of capital gains. The foundation's 14% administrative cost ratio is the problem; recommends routing grants under $25,000 through the DAF and consolidating grantees.

items.title: Ten-year cash flow for retired business owners, revised for a lake house purchase
items.summary: Revision of a November 2025 projection after the clients decided to buy a $1.9 million lake house. Shows the net portfolio draw rising from 2.1% to 3.5%, at the firm's sustainability ceiling, and recommends liquidating $1 million of high-basis lots and borrowing $900,000 on a pledged-asset line rather than selling appreciated holdings. Includes a Roth conversion window before required distributions begin.

items.title: Five-year cash flow for a dual-income family facing an RSU cliff
items.summary: Projection for a household with $612,000 of income, $132,000 of it RSU vesting that ends in 2028. Base-case savings capacity of about $108,000 a year falls to $44,000 if both children move to independent school, and turns negative from 2029 after the vesting cliff unless spending adjusts. Recommends funding 401(k)s and 529s while the vesting lasts and holding six months of spend in cash.

items.title: Estate and liquidity review for a founder with a concentrated stock position
items.summary: For a household with 48% of investable assets in one low-basis stock. Recommends a 10b5-1 plan selling 10% of the holding a year, a two-year GRAT funded with shares, moving a $10 million second-to-die policy into an ILIT, and making all charitable gifts in shares. Liquidity buffer of 14 months is adequate but eroding at the current spending growth rate.

items.title: Credit card spend analysis, dual-income family with young children
items.summary: Full-year review of $187,000 of card spend across three cards for a two-earner household with two children. Found nine unused subscriptions ($2,340 a year), 412,000 unredeemed points, and dining growing 22% year on year. Recommends consolidating to two cards, redeeming points before the next devaluation, and a travel budget. The categorisation follows version 2 of the firm's standard; the charitable line needs the giving team's treatment of a gala table.

items.summary: Interactive model for a couple in their late twenties with $120,000 saved, comparing renting against buying a $650,000 condo over seven years. items.summary: Review of $96,000 of annual card spend for a retired couple, 44% of it travel including a six-week trip paid on a card with a 3% foreign transaction fee and no travel insurance. items.title: Student loan repayment options for a physician finishing residency
items.summary: For a resident with $310,000 of federal loans moving to an attending salary of $340,000. Compares Public Service Loan Forgiveness at a non-profit hospital against refinancing at a private practice, with the income jump modelled year by year. The forgiveness path wins by about $95,000 if the client stays in qualifying employment for the remaining five years; refinancing wins if they leave within two.
